prayerExcerpt.en-US: I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore I die in exile.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Amei a justiça e odiei a iniquidade; por isso morro no exílio.

meta.face: A small, spare Tuscan of about sixty-five with an olive, sun-darkened complexion and a SHORT, COMPACT face — broad across the brow and cheekbones and short from brow to chin, ending in a firm, slightly jutting small chin; a short, strongly arched, beak-like nose; small, black, intensely bright and piercing eyes under straight, dark, bristling brows drawn a little together; a thin, tight-set, determined mouth; a very short, close-trimmed iron-grey beard and moustache; a little iron-grey hair showing under the tiara; a keen, unflinching gaze.
meta.basis: Contemporaries, friend and foe, remembered Hildebrand as small, swarthy and keen-eyed (Hugh of Cluny noted his small stature; Durant sums him up as "small of stature, homely of feature, keen of eye"); the Exultet roll of his time shows him in a tall conical tiara. We keep the stature, colouring and eyes and idealise the rest.
meta.excerpt: His last words at Salerno, 1085, as quoted verbatim in the Catholic Encyclopedia (1909), "Pope St. Gregory VII" (https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/06791c.htm; local copy consult/batch-12/catholic-encyclopedia-gregory-vii.html); Latin "Dilexi iustitiam et odivi iniquitatem, propterea morior in exilio"; pt-BR is our faithful rendering. The calendar entry sanctorale.05-25.gregory-vii has no formulary.
